exclusion_quote: Dissertation at Uppsala University to be publicly examined in Polhemsalen, Ångström-laboratoriet, Thursday, September 23, 2004 at 10:15 for the Degree of Doctor of Philosophy.

I1.quote: The mass of the ANPC and MWNB samples investigated were 2.0124 g and 0.4717 g, respectively. The isotherms were measured at three temperatures (77, 195 and 300 K) in a UHV compatible Sievert’s apparatus.

I2.quote: The hydrogen uptake of two nanostructured carbon based materials denoted Multi-Walled Nano-Barrels (MWNB) and Amorphous Nanoporous Carbon (ANPC) was explored. [...] The materials used were synthesized through a selective etching procedure with SiC and Al4C3 as precursors.

I3.quote: The maximum hydrogen uptake at 77 K and hydrogen pressure of 10 MPa was determined to be 4.2 and 6.2 wt.% for ANPC and MWNB, respectively.

I4.quote: The resulting materials exhibited a high porosity and large specific surface area (1000 m2·g for ANPC and 600 m2·g for MWNB)

I5.quote: The dissociative and non-dissociative hydrogen uptake in carbon nanostructures and metallic films were investigated by measurements and analysis of solubility isotherms.

notes: Document is a doctoral dissertation (comprehensive summary, Acta Universitatis Upsaliensis 1005, 2004); the PDF holds the summary only, not the reprinted papers. I1-I3 met by the author's own Sieverts measurements on carbide-derived carbons (ANPC from SiC/Al4C3 chlorination, MWNB); I4 met by the surface areas in Section 4.1 (BET-N2 named as the standard method in Section 3.3.1, p. 43). First applicable code in §4 order is not_primary (thesis). The carbon H2 data are summarized from Paper I (J. Alloy. Comp. 330-332, 670 (2002)), per 'This thesis is based on the papers given below' (p. 7), so duplicate_data would also likely apply, but not_primary precedes it.
